title: Boot registry seal
statement: The kernel shall register application threads only before start, within a configured finite capacity, using permanent caller-provided control blocks and stacks.
rationale: Prevent runtime acquisition and ambiguous lifetime.
acceptance: Exactly RTOS_MAX_THREADS unique registrations succeed; duplicate, excess and post-start calls fail unchanged; zero application threads starts idle.
verification: Host capacity/duplicate tests and target registration API/seal tests.
configuration: RTOS_MAX_THREADS 1..255.
resource_budget: Configured application pointer table plus one private idle thread.
finding: create checks running state and add checks capacity/duplicates; existing tests cover helpers, not target boot sealing.

title: Static resource lifetimes
statement: The kernel shall retain boot resource ownership metadata through shutdown and neither allocate nor free general heap storage during initialization or execution.
rationale: Completion must not leak or silently recycle resources.
acceptance: Firmware passes no-heap audit; repeated completion, IPC, timer and network operations preserve capacities and storage addresses; finished storage stays reserved.
verification: ELF audit, ownership review and target resource-inventory stress.
configuration: All enabled features.
resource_budget: Zero general heap bytes; boot-fixed capacities.
finding: Thread retains caller storage metadata and exit marks finished; runtime lifecycle stress evidence is absent.

title: Stack registration bounds
statement: Registration shall reject invalid stack alignment, insufficient size, address overflow and stack/control-block overlap before changing state.
rationale: Prevent corruption during boot.
acceptance: Reject size below 512, size/alignment not divisible by 16, overflowing ranges and overlap; accept touching ranges; failures preserve registry/control contents.
verification: Host boundary tests and target registration failure atomicity.
configuration: Minimum 512 bytes; alignment 16.
resource_budget: One scan of configured registered ranges.
finding: create checks ranges before registration; existing helper tests cover only selected boundary cases.

title: Strict priority dispatch
statement: At each dispatch the scheduler shall select the ready application thread with greatest effective priority and use idle only when no application is ready.
rationale: Predictable priority semantics.
acceptance: Finite reference-model comparison never selects a lower ready priority; priority-zero work precedes idle; higher-priority wakeup wins next dispatch.
verification: Host small-state model and target wakeup/idle tests.
configuration: Priorities 0..255; larger first.
resource_budget: At most RTOS_MAX_THREADS candidates per selection.
finding: pick compares one priority field and trap provides separate idle; effective/base separation is not implemented.

title: Equal-priority fairness
statement: Timer round robin shall rotate equal-priority ready peers when enabled; explicit yield shall rotate peers in either configuration.
rationale: Sharing without mandatory time slicing.
acceptance: N ready peers each run once in N rotations; slicing disabled retains current peer unless higher priority ready; yield rotates in both modes.
verification: Peer counts, cursor wrap, blocked peers and target timer slicing tests.
configuration: RTOS_ROUND_ROBIN = 0 or 1.
resource_budget: Existing registry and one cursor; no extra allocations.
finding: pick supports retention and cursor rotation; trap forces ECALL rotation independently of timer slicing.

title: Priority changes
statement: The priority API shall atomically update a registered live thread base priority and reconsider scheduling before returning when running while preserving active inheritance.
rationale: Separate selected and donated priority.
acceptance: Unregistered/finished fail unchanged; boot/sleeping changes succeed; lowering current permits higher-priority peer before return; preserve donations.
verification: Target priority changes, invalid IDs, sleeping and donated-priority cases.
configuration: Base/effective priorities 0..255.
resource_budget: Recomputation bounded by thread/mutex capacities.
finding: set_priority checks membership and finished state then yields; Thread has only one priority field.

title: Integer context preservation
statement: The RISCue trap boundary shall preserve interrupted integer registers, continuation PC, stack pointer and machine status across preemption and yields with 16-byte C++ call alignment.
rationale: Asynchronous state requires assembly capture.
acceptance: Distinct register patterns survive 100000 timer preemptions and yields with zero PC, stack, register or interrupt-state mismatches.
verification: Assembly-assisted target register stress with nested C++ calls and canaries.
configuration: Single-hart RV32 integer machine mode; no FP/vector.
resource_budget: 144-byte frame plus analyzed kernel call depth.
finding: Save/restore offsets match initial 36-word frame by inspection; no executable target stress test exists.

title: Inline assembly compiler contracts
statement: CSR and critical-section inline assembly shall declare correct operands and ordering; standalone assembly shall be limited to startup and asynchronous entry/restore.
rationale: Optimization-safe register allocation.
acceptance: Every supported optimized configuration preserves context/API results; disassembly retains approved CSR operands and ordering.
verification: Compiler/disassembly review and target optimization/LTO matrix when supported.
configuration: Documented optimization/compiler configurations.
resource_budget: No new runtime storage; fixed assembly boundaries.
finding: Inline CSR operands/clobbers exist; optimization-matrix runtime evidence is absent.

title: Relative sleep wrap semantics
statement: Relative sleep shall accept 0..INT32_MAX ticks, treat zero as yield, reject larger delays and use wrap-safe deadlines.
rationale: Avoid ambiguous modular comparisons.
acceptance: Cover 0, 1, INT32_MAX, INT32_MAX+1 and wrap across UINT32_MAX; rejected calls do not block or mutate state.
verification: Host modular arithmetic and target sleep API boundary tests.
configuration: 32-bit ticks; relative delay at most INT32_MAX.
resource_budget: One deadline/thread; one bounded wake scan.
finding: sleep_for enforces half-range and advance compares modularly; tests cover helper wrap cases only.

title: Delayed timer catch-up
statement: Timer handling shall compute missed periods arithmetically, scan sleepers once per delivered interrupt and reject catch-up beyond the modular horizon.
rationale: Interrupt work must not scale with missed periods.
acceptance: 1, 10, 1000000 missed periods require one scan with model-equivalent wakes; greater than INT32_MAX invokes fault policy.
verification: Scan-count instrumentation and masked-interrupt/exact-boundary/horizon target tests.
configuration: Nonzero integer timer period; half-range horizon.
resource_budget: One arithmetic catch-up and one thread scan.
finding: elapsed_ticks uses division and trap advances once, halting above INT32_MAX; target evidence absent.

title: Timer MMIO integrity
statement: The timer port shall read a coherent 64-bit monotonic clock and update compare without exposing a transient earlier deadline.
rationale: RV32 split-word MMIO is non-atomic.
acceptance: Rollover reads are coherent; compare writes high-max, low, final-high; diagnostics report actual integer period.
verification: Instrumented MMIO and target rollover/write-order tests.
configuration: Timer/compare addresses and supplied clock/tick rates.
resource_budget: Three compare writes; read retry assumptions documented for hardware.
finding: time_now retries high/low/high and arm uses safe write order; no MMIO execution test exists.

title: Absolute periodic release
statement: The kernel shall provide absolute sleep and a static periodic helper advancing from prior intended deadlines with missed-release reporting.
rationale: Relative sleeps accumulate execution drift.
acceptance: Variable work preserves original release grid; overdue activity skips to next future release and counts misses; reject zero/half-range-invalid periods; support wrap.
verification: On-time, missed-release, wrap and invalid-period tests.
configuration: Optional helper; period 1..INT32_MAX; saturating miss counter.
resource_budget: Fixed state per boot-created periodic activity.
finding: Only relative sleep exists; tick-boundary rounding does not supply a drift-free release grid.

title: Interrupt-state restoration
statement: Kernel-private critical sections shall preserve prior interrupt state across internal scheduler transitions; while scheduling is active, public blocking or scheduling calls shall reject application-disabled interrupt context before changing thread state.
rationale: Blocking/nesting must not enable MIE accidentally.
acceptance: Nested private locks restore prior MIE without enabling early. Internal sleep/resume preserves its private lock state. Application-held interrupt masking followed by sleep, yield, exit or a rescheduling priority change is rejected through a documented error or fault without a partial state transition; pre-start boot configuration remains legal.
verification: Target nested-lock/blocking/preemption MIE observation.
configuration: Single hart; no implicit interrupt nesting.
resource_budget: One saved status word per lock; nesting bounded by reviewed call depth.
finding: Lock restores only prior enabled MIE; saved sleeping context can remain disabled until destructor resumes. Builder 25 distinguished internal transition locks from application-held masking; current public APIs do not enforce this context policy.

title: Interrupt dispatcher boundary
statement: The port shall dispatch registered supported sources, acknowledge through a board contract and route unsupported sources/exceptions to bounded fault handling.
rationale: Verify external IRQ boundary before drivers enable it.
acceptance: One handler/source; invalid/spurious IDs cannot call arbitrary memory or loop indefinitely; acknowledgment permits subsequent interrupts.
verification: External, invalid, spurious, disabled and repeated acknowledgment tests.
configuration: Fixed boot source capacity and board acknowledgment operations.
resource_budget: Fixed source table and bounded handling/acknowledgment.
finding: rtos_trap handles ECALL/timer only and halts other causes; external dispatcher is absent.

title: Deferred interrupt work
statement: Drivers shall signal boot-created deferred workers through explicit ISR APIs with fixed storage and bounded nonblocking operations.
rationale: Keep top-half interrupt work analyzable.
acceptance: No ISR allocation/wait; full capacity returns result and increments overflow; accepted work wakes worker without lost signals.
verification: Burst, full, coalescing, wakeup and forbidden blocking-context tests.
configuration: Optional worker count, queue capacity and coalescing policy.
resource_budget: Boot worker stacks and fixed pending-work slots.
finding: Current APIs explicitly disallow ISR calls and offer no deferred worker/wakeup facility.

title: Static mutex ownership
statement: Boot-initialized mutexes shall enforce a single owner, reject non-owner unlock and provide nonrecursive try, timed and blocking acquisition.
rationale: Establish ownership before inheritance.
acceptance: One owner maximum; recursive acquisition reports error; timeout/unlock races preserve ownership; invalid/ISR/pre-start calls leave state consistent.
verification: Contention, recursion, wrong-owner, timeout-race and context-misuse tests.
configuration: Optional fixed mutex capacity; nonrecursive initially.
resource_budget: One owner/control record per mutex; bounded thread waiters.
finding: No mutex API exists; synchronization remains explicitly a future extension.

title: Transitive priority inheritance
statement: Mutex contention shall raise effective priorities to active donation maxima, propagate through bounded chains and recompute when donations end.
rationale: Bound medium-priority interference during inversion.
acceptance: H/L contention preempts M; H/L/X propagation works; timeout, unlock and base-priority changes recompute every held mutex without stale donations.
verification: H/M/L, chained, multiple-owner, withdrawal and base-priority change tests.
configuration: Mutex inheritance with priorities 0..255.
resource_budget: Traversal bounded by thread/mutex capacities; static graph storage.
finding: Thread has one priority and no donation/ownership graph; transitive inheritance is absent.

title: Mutex deadlock and owner termination
statement: Mutex acquisition shall detect wait-for cycles before blocking, and owner exit shall fault deterministically without silently releasing ownership.
rationale: Inheritance cannot repair deadlock/protected data.
acceptance: Two/three-thread cycles return deadlock; maximum-depth search terminates; owner return/exit records fault without ownership transfer.
verification: Cycle, maximum-chain and owner-return/exit fault tests.
configuration: Documented deadlock error and owner-exit fault policy.
resource_budget: At most RTOS_MAX_THREADS search nodes; fixed fault storage.
finding: exit unconditionally marks finished without owned-object validation; mutex owner termination needs an explicit policy.

title: Counting and binary semaphores
statement: Static semaphores shall enforce maximum count and offer try, timed, blocking take and bounded thread/ISR release with overflow results.
rationale: Ownership-free finite synchronization.
acceptance: Count within 0..max; overflow fails; timeout/release resolves exactly once; priority waiters and ISR rescheduling follow policy.
verification: Zero/max/overflow, waiter ordering, timeout-race and ISR tests.
configuration: Optional boot counts/max; binary maximum 1.
resource_budget: Fixed records and one wait membership/thread.
finding: Existing wake logic handles sleeping only; no counting object or ISR release exists.

title: Atomic bounded wait lifecycle
statement: Blocking primitives shall atomically register waiters, transition state and resolve wakeup, timeout or cancellation exactly once in fixed waiter storage.
rationale: Prevent lost wakeups and duplicate readiness.
acceptance: Signal-before/after-enqueue and timeout ties resolve once; no duplicate memberships; capacity never exceeds thread count.
verification: Deterministic scheduling/reference interleavings and repeated reuse.
configuration: Shared substrate for all blocking features.
resource_budget: One active wait record/thread; bounded object wait queues.
finding: State lacks generic blocked/wait-reason fields and signal/timeout arbitration.

title: Event flags semantics
statement: Enabled event groups shall support a configured width of 1..32 bits, a boot-declared reserved-bit mask, any/all waits, and optional clear-on-exit evaluated in descending effective priority with FIFO ordering among equal-priority waiters.
rationale: Avoid ambiguous flag consumption.
acceptance: Reject masks outside the configured width or containing reserved bits. Process waiters in priority/FIFO order against the remaining flags. For a satisfied clear-on-exit waiter, consume requested bits currently set (any) or all requested bits (all) before evaluating the next waiter; nonclearing waiters leave flags unchanged. Exhaustive 3-bit models cover consumption, simultaneous waiters and timeout/ISR-set races.
verification: Small-width exhaustive combinations, multiwaiter, timeout and ISR-set tests.
configuration: RTOS_EVENT_BITS = 1..32; boot reserved mask; priority/FIFO waiter order; explicit clear-on-exit.
resource_budget: Fixed flag/control record per group; bounded thread waiters.
finding: No event group API exists; sleep arithmetic alone does not specify consumption semantics. Builder 25 resolved previously unspecified consumption and waiter ordering policies.

title: Typed fixed-capacity queues
statement: Queues shall hold a compile-time bounded number of trivially copyable messages in caller storage with FIFO send/receive and full, empty, timeout results.
rationale: Avoid allocation and payload destructors.
acceptance: Capacity N accepts exactly N pending messages; FIFO survives wrap/multiple producers/consumers; rejected sends preserve data; invalid types/sizes/alignment fail compilation.
verification: Capacity 1/N, wrap, full/empty, concurrency, payload and compile-fail tests.
configuration: Optional payload type and positive static capacity.
resource_budget: N times payload bytes plus fixed metadata and bounded waiters.
finding: Byte copy support exists but queues and payload-lifetime contracts do not.

title: ISR-safe queue subset
statement: ISR queues shall use explicit nonblocking APIs, bounded copies, immediate capacity errors and interrupt-return higher-priority rescheduling.
rationale: Do not reuse blocking APIs from ISR.
acceptance: Maximum copy bounded; failed full/empty leaves state intact; accepted messages survive IRQ/consumer races; highest-ready worker runs next legal return.
verification: Maximum-payload, full/empty, interleaving, scheduling and misuse tests.
configuration: Explicit ISR subset and maximum payload bytes.
resource_budget: One configured bounded payload copy and fixed metadata changes.
finding: Current APIs are thread-only; no distinct ISR queue API exists.

title: Static software timers
statement: Software timers shall use boot-reserved records, one-shot/periodic modes, bounded expiration processing and boot-created callback workers outside ISR.
rationale: Callbacks must not extend timer interrupt latency unpredictably.
acceptance: Capacity exhaustion returns an error. Periodic timers retain the intended release grid and allow at most one pending invocation per timer; excess expirations coalesce and increment a saturating 32-bit unsigned missed-expiration counter. Cancellation of a queued but not executing callback prevents its start and returns Cancelled. Cancellation during execution returns Busy without changing its schedule; caller may retry. Cancel/restart/expire races produce exactly one documented result; callbacks run only in worker context.
verification: Capacity, cancel/expire, restart, wrap, long-callback, backlog and context tests.
configuration: Optional timer count and worker priority/stack; one pending callback per timer; 32-bit unsigned saturating miss counter; explicit Cancelled/Busy results.
resource_budget: Fixed records/callback queue; scan bounded by configured timer count.
finding: Timer trap handles ticks/sleepers only; software timer registry and callback worker are absent. Builder 25 selected one-invocation coalescing and explicit cancellation results.

title: Bounded work and timing evidence
statement: Every kernel API and IRQ path shall document work bounds, forbid unbounded callbacks under interrupt masking and expose measured dispatch/interrupt-disabled latency per supported release profile.
rationale: Small code is not a latency guarantee.
acceptance: Every operation has a finite count-based bound; max-capacity reports pin compiler, configuration, workload and observed durations; explicit application thresholds gate release without a formal WCET claim.
verification: Instrument worst capacities, wait chains, snapshot sizes and timer backlog on target; archive logs.
configuration: All supported profiles; application-defined latency thresholds.
resource_budget: Bounds use fixed thread, mutex, timer, queue and snapshot capacities; fixed instrumentation storage.
finding: Docs identify linear scans and pending timing gates; measured target latency evidence is absent.

title: Boot device registry
statement: The device registry shall accept unique boot-defined names and static driver objects before sealing at scheduler start.
rationale: Drivers currently require single-owner integration without a common registry.
acceptance: Duplicate names, null operation tables, capacity overflow and post-start registration fail unchanged; lookup returns the exact registered instance or not-found.
verification: Registry capacity, duplicate, seal and lookup tests.
configuration: Optional devices; positive maximum device count; names at most 31 bytes.
resource_budget: Fixed registry entries and copied bounded names; zero runtime allocation.
finding: Driver guidance reserves objects statically but no device registry API exists.

title: Unified device operations
statement: Devices shall expose bounded read, write and typed control operations returning status and transferred byte count, with explicit nonblocking or absolute-deadline modes.
rationale: A consistent contract avoids per-driver ambiguity and indefinite calls.
acceptance: Unsupported operations return not-supported; zero-length operations transfer zero; short transfers report exact progress; expired deadlines never wait; control rejects unknown commands and incorrect payload sizes unchanged.
verification: Mock-driver short transfer, unsupported, deadline and control validation tests.
configuration: Fixed operation table per device; finite control command set.
resource_budget: Caller buffers accessed only during synchronous ownership; abort-uncertain DMA uses fixed driver-owned staging; request state and concurrent operations boot-bounded.
finding: Ethernet has explicit busy/error callback contracts but no general read/write/control interface exists. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Bounded descriptor handles
statement: Opening a device or file shall acquire a slot from a boot-reserved descriptor table and return an index-plus-generation handle.
rationale: Unix-style handles need finite capacity and stale-reference protection.
acceptance: Exactly configured slot count opens succeed; excess returns resource-exhausted; close/reopen invalidates old handles; generations never wrap into reuse because exhausted-generation slots retire until reboot.
verification: Exhaustion, stale handle, invalid index and near-generation-limit tests.
configuration: Optional descriptors; configured slot count; 32-bit generation.
resource_budget: Fixed descriptor records; no heap; retired slots remain counted unavailable.
finding: Current API exposes Thread pointers only; no descriptor table or generation management exists.

title: Descriptor close lifecycle
statement: Close shall mark a valid descriptor closing, reject new operations, wait only until its supplied deadline for in-flight operations and release the slot exactly once after quiescence.
rationale: Freeing slots during active driver access would corrupt ownership.
acceptance: Close after successful completion returns invalid-handle. Concurrent close while another close call is active returns Busy. A timed-out close retains Closing state and permits a later same-handle close retry after the first call returns. New I/O is rejected in Closing. Quiescent cleanup releases the slot exactly once; driver-close failure quarantines a diagnosable unavailable slot.
verification: Close versus read/write races, timeout retry and injected close-failure tests.
configuration: Finite per-slot active-operation counter; close uses absolute deadline.
resource_budget: Fixed closing state and active count per descriptor; no detached cleanup allocation.
finding: Existing ownership guidance does not define descriptor teardown or concurrent close. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Bounded pathname resolution
statement: The VFS shall accept explicit bounded byte-span paths, normalize absolute paths with repeated separators and dot components, and reject embedded NUL bytes, traversal above root and symbolic links.
rationale: A small namespace must avoid recursive and unbounded resolution.
acceptance: Validate the complete supplied byte span, including bytes after any embedded NUL. Reject excessive span/component lengths before provider calls. /a/../b resolves to /b; /../b and relative paths fail invalid-path; no symbolic links are followed.
verification: Path normalization model and malformed/boundary input tests.
configuration: Optional VFS; positive maximum path bytes, component bytes and component count.
resource_budget: Fixed normalization workspace per configured concurrent resolver; traversal bounded by component count.
finding: No pathname API or VFS configuration exists; static memory rules require bounded resolver workspace. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Static device filesystem
statement: A devfs provider shall expose sealed device-registry entries under /dev and route opens through descriptor ownership rules.
rationale: The accepted Unix-style device namespace should reuse registry identity.
acceptance: Every registered exported device appears once; unknown names return not-found; directory iteration is bounded and stable; create, unlink and rename return read-only.
verification: Registry-to-devfs mapping, stable enumeration and forbidden mutation tests.
configuration: Optional devfs; boot export flag per device.
resource_budget: No duplicated driver objects; at most one fixed directory record per exported device.
finding: Drivers are listed in documentation but /dev has no implementation.

title: Read-only ROM filesystem
statement: A ROM filesystem shall expose a boot-linked immutable file table with bounded offset reads and no executable loading.
rationale: Static assets and help text need file access without writable storage complexity.
acceptance: Reads at EOF return zero; short tail reads are exact; overflowing offsets and invalid table ranges fail; all writes and namespace mutations return read-only; content bytes match linked assets.
verification: ROM image table validation, offset boundaries and content checksum tests.
configuration: Optional ROMFS; fixed file count and linked asset byte budget.
resource_budget: Immutable table and linked bytes; per-open offset stored in descriptor slot.
finding: The linker builds one static firmware image; no filesystem or executable loader exists.

title: Bounded RAM filesystem
statement: Optional RAMFS shall use boot-reserved inode and data-block pools, permit only regular files and directories and return explicit exhaustion without growing storage.
rationale: Writable temporary files must preserve the no-heap contract.
acceptance: Inode/block exhaustion leaves existing contents intact; writes may return documented exact short counts; unlink of open files reclaims blocks only after last close; truncate zeroes newly visible bytes; reboot discards contents.
verification: Pool exhaustion, short write, open-unlink, truncate and repeated create/delete conservation tests.
configuration: Optional RAMFS; fixed inode count, block size, block count and directory-entry capacity.
resource_budget: Exactly configured inode, directory and block pools; ownership counters conserve every slot.
finding: Memory helpers exist but no writable filesystem or fixed block ownership manager exists.

title: Boot mount table
statement: Mounts shall be registered only at boot with unique absolute normalized prefixes, then remain immutable; resolution shall select the longest component-boundary prefix.
rationale: Immutable mounting keeps lookup and provider lifetime bounded.
acceptance: Duplicate prefixes and mount-table overflow fail; /rom does not match /romance; nested mount chooses longest match; runtime mount/unmount returns sealed.
verification: Prefix boundary, nested mount, duplicate, capacity and boot seal tests.
configuration: Fixed mount count; optional devfs, ROMFS and RAMFS providers.
resource_budget: Fixed mount table and bounded copied prefixes; lookup scans at most configured mounts.
finding: There are no current mount options; configuration guidance requires lifecycle and budgets before exposure.

title: Static byte pipes
statement: A pipe shall use a boot-reserved byte ring and bounded endpoint slots, provide partial FIFO transfers and resolve endpoint closure without dynamic allocation.
rationale: Pipes provide useful Unix-style composition without processes.
acceptance: Empty pipe with writers returns would-block or waits to deadline; empty pipe without writers returns EOF; write without readers returns broken-pipe; close wakes affected waiters; byte order survives ring wrap.
verification: Ring wrap, full/empty, deadline, endpoint-close races and endpoint exhaustion tests.
configuration: Optional pipes; fixed pipe count, bytes per pipe and reader/writer endpoint limits.
resource_budget: Fixed rings and endpoint records; total queued bytes never exceeds configured storage.
finding: No pipe API exists; static byte storage and exact endpoint teardown must be added.

title: Built-in command registry
statement: The shell shall dispatch only a sealed boot-defined table of built-in C++ command functions with unique bounded names.
rationale: A Unix-like console need not load programs or create processes.
acceptance: Duplicate/overlong names fail at boot; unknown commands return command-not-found; dispatch invokes only registered pointers; registry overflow fails unchanged.
verification: Registry validation, unknown command and dispatch identity tests.
configuration: Optional shell; fixed command count and maximum command-name bytes.
resource_budget: Fixed command table; all command code linked into firmware.
finding: Firmware is statically linked and no shell registry or process loader exists.

title: Bounded shell parser
statement: The shell shall parse bounded lines with whitespace separation, single/double quoted arguments and backslash escapes, rejecting unsupported expansion, redirection and pipeline syntax initially.
rationale: Explicit small grammar avoids accidental unbounded Unix-shell expectations.
acceptance: Reject oversized lines, excessive arguments, unmatched quotes and trailing escapes before execution. Preserve quoted spaces and empty arguments. Unquoted expansion, redirection and pipeline metacharacters return parse errors; quoted or escaped metacharacters are literal bytes and never trigger expansion or execution.
verification: Grammar corpus, boundary tests and deterministic fuzzing against reference parser.
configuration: Fixed maximum line bytes and argument count; no environment expansion or command substitution.
resource_budget: One fixed line buffer and argument-index array per shell session.
finding: No parser exists; caller-owned storage policy rules out dynamically growing argument vectors. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Static shell sessions
statement: Each enabled shell session shall own boot-reserved input/output buffers and a boot-created worker, with bounded editing and output backpressure.
rationale: Console convenience must not consume unbounded kernel memory or stall unrelated threads.
acceptance: Session capacity is fixed; line overflow discards until newline and reports one error; output waits only to deadline and reports truncation; disconnected sessions release no borrowed buffer prematurely.
verification: Maximum sessions, oversized line recovery, slow output and disconnect tests.
configuration: Fixed session count, worker priority/stack and input/output ring bytes.
resource_budget: Exactly configured session buffers and stacks; no runtime worker creation.
finding: Current kernel seals thread creation at start, so interactive sessions require boot-created workers.

title: Jobs on boot workers
statement: Background commands shall run only on a fixed boot-created worker pool with generation-tagged job slots and cooperative cancellation.
rationale: Provide limited jobs without fork, executable loading or runtime stacks.
acceptance: Pool exhaustion returns Busy. Jobs run on permanent workers that return to their dispatch loop, never exit. Generation-tagged stale IDs fail; generation-exhausted slots retire until reboot. Cancellation is cooperative without forced unwinding; uncooperative jobs remain occupied and become Stuck after the configured grace interval.
verification: Pool exhaustion, stale IDs, completion/cancel races and noncooperating-job tests.
configuration: Optional jobs; fixed worker/job count, stacks and cancellation grace ticks.
resource_budget: One permanent stack/control block per worker plus fixed job records and bounded copied arguments.
finding: create is boot-only and exit does not unwind active objects; background work cannot safely imply dynamic tasks or forced cancellation. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Bounded diagnostic commands
statement: Built-in ps, top, uptime and devices commands shall consume coherent bounded snapshots and print explicit truncation indicators without holding kernel locks during formatting or output.
rationale: Existing thread metrics should become usable from the console without long masked I/O.
acceptance: ps reports name/state/base/effective priority; top handles zero elapsed time and disabled metrics explicitly; rows never exceed caller capacity; slow console output occurs after snapshot lock release.
verification: Snapshot-to-command golden outputs, truncation, disabled metrics and slow-console instrumentation.
configuration: Optional diagnostics; fixed maximum rows and output bytes per command invocation.
resource_budget: Fixed snapshot rows and formatting buffer per session; one snapshot per refresh.
finding: snapshot already returns bounded rows and priority/runtime fields; no shell commands or base/effective split exists.

title: UART bounded transport
statement: The UART driver shall use fixed RX/TX rings, expose nonblocking/deadline transfers and defer interrupt processing through approved bounded paths.
rationale: UART is the documented first board addition and console prerequisite.
acceptance: RX overflow drops newest byte and increments a saturating counter; TX full returns short count or waits only to deadline; framing/parity/overrun errors are counted; loopback preserves accepted byte order.
verification: Hardware/model loopback, ring saturation, error injection and deadline tests.
configuration: Optional UART instances; fixed ring bytes, baud and framing selected at boot.
resource_budget: Fixed per-instance rings/control state; ISR work capped at configured bytes per interrupt.
finding: Driver inventory proposes UART rings and loopback tests; no UART implementation exists.

title: Console routing and fault output
statement: Console input/output shall route to one boot-selected device; panic output shall use a bounded polling path with a fixed byte/time limit and no descriptor locks.
rationale: Diagnostics must remain bounded when scheduler or locks fail.
acceptance: Normal output follows device backpressure; panic writes at most configured bytes and stops at deadline or unavailable device; recursive panic terminates immediately without lock acquisition.
verification: Slow/stuck UART, recursive panic and scheduler-disabled output tests.
configuration: One boot console; optional panic output with positive byte and tick/cycle limits.
resource_budget: Fixed panic buffer and recursion flag; no worker or memory acquisition in panic.
finding: stop currently disables interrupts and loops; no console routing or bounded emergency output exists.

title: GPIO ownership and safe state
statement: GPIO shall enforce boot-declared pin ownership, validated direction/functions and board-defined safe output values on failed initialization or explicit shutdown.
rationale: Uncoordinated register access can affect unrelated pins and unsafe outputs.
acceptance: Conflicting claims and unsupported pin/function fail before hardware changes; writes affect only owned pins; output values are established before enabling drive; failure restores declared safe state.
verification: Mock-register ownership/mask tests and board safe-state measurements.
configuration: Optional fixed pin table and owner map; board safe values required for outputs.
resource_budget: One fixed record per declared pin; no runtime pin claims.
finding: Inventory requests pin ownership and atomic register semantics but no GPIO contract is implemented.

title: SPI bounded transactions
statement: SPI shall accept transactions from fixed boot request slots, serialize each bus and hold chip select only for one bounded transaction with an absolute completion deadline.
rationale: Bus sharing and chip-select lifetime require explicit ownership.
acceptance: Validate mode/rate/length before assertion; preserve segment order; queue full returns busy; timeout deasserts chip select and returns transferred count; subsequent requests recover or receive unavailable.
verification: Mode validation, contention, full queue, timeout and chip-select waveform tests.
configuration: Optional buses; fixed request count, maximum segments/bytes and supported rates/modes.
resource_budget: Fixed request/control slots and boot driver-owned DMA staging; hardware cannot retain caller or stack buffer references after any return, including errors.
finding: SPI inventory lists slots, chip-select ownership and timeouts without an implemented driver. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: I2C error and recovery bounds
statement: I2C shall serialize bounded address transactions, report NACK/arbitration/timeout distinctly and attempt at most nine recovery clocks followed by STOP before marking a stuck bus unavailable.
rationale: A stuck peripheral must not block a worker indefinitely.
acceptance: Invalid addresses/lengths fail before START; repeated-start sequences preserve atomic ownership; NACK returns exact progress; recovery is attempted once per failed transaction and never exceeds deadline; unavailable buses reject requests until explicit bounded reinitialize.
verification: NACK, arbitration loss, clock stretch, stuck SDA and recovery waveform tests.
configuration: Optional buses; fixed request count/bytes; standard 7-bit addressing initially.
resource_budget: Fixed transaction slots and one bus recovery state per instance.
finding: I2C inventory identifies NACK/stuck-bus concerns but defines no recovery bound or implementation.

title: Progress-based watchdog supervision
statement: A boot-created supervisor shall feed the hardware watchdog only when every enabled critical thread advances its registered progress token within its configured monotonic interval.
rationale: Timer interrupts alone do not demonstrate application progress.
acceptance: A stuck critical worker prevents feeding by its deadline; token wrap is handled; noncritical workers do not inhibit feeding; first missed participant is recorded before reset; watchdog setup is validated against supervisor period.
verification: Stalled worker, interrupt-only activity, token wrap, false-positive margin and actual reset tests.
configuration: Optional supervisor; fixed critical participant list and positive per-participant deadlines.
resource_budget: Fixed token/deadline records plus one boot supervisor stack; one scan per supervision period.
finding: Documentation recommends progress-based feeding and reset records; no supervisor or watchdog driver exists.

title: Ordered driver boot failure
statement: Drivers shall initialize through a fixed dependency-ordered boot table; critical failure shall abort startup and reverse-unwind every initialized driver, while optional failure shall clean up that partially initialized driver, skip transitive dependents and retain successful providers.
rationale: Partial initialization must not leave workers using unavailable hardware.
acceptance: Reject cycles and unknown dependencies before hardware access. Run partial-driver cleanup even when initialization fails. Critical failure prevents start and cleans initialized drivers once in reverse order. Optional failure cleans only the failed partial driver, skips dependents and retains initialized shared providers. Every cleanup has a deadline; cleanup failure records a fault and preserves safe/unavailable state.
verification: Dependency graph validation and failure injection at every boot-table position.
configuration: Fixed init entry count; critical/optional classification and bounded init/shutdown deadlines.
resource_budget: Fixed table and visited/state arrays; traversal bounded by configured entries/edges.
finding: Boot/recovery backlog proposes ordered init and partial-start tests but start has no driver dependency orchestration. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Device request cancellation
statement: Timed device operations shall return only after hardware has no reference to caller buffers; abort-uncertain DMA hardware shall use boot driver-owned staging or fail driver initialization, and failed abort shall quarantine its request/staging slot.
rationale: Timeout alone cannot make asynchronous buffer reuse safe.
acceptance: Both success and fault returns leave caller storage safe to reuse. Abort-uncertain hardware never receives caller addresses. Failed abort retains only driver-owned staging and quarantines it with a distinct fault result. Late completions cannot target reused generations; repeated abort is idempotent.
verification: Delayed DMA completion, abort success/failure, stale completion and slot quarantine tests.
configuration: Fixed abort deadline and request-generation width; asynchronous drivers use driver-owned buffers.
resource_budget: Fixed request slots and staging buffers; quarantined capacity never silently reused.
finding: Ethernet explicitly forbids retaining caller TX pointers; broader timed/DMA operation cancellation is unspecified. Builder50 refined lifecycle, buffer ownership or parser/boot policy before implementation.

title: Bounded readiness polling
statement: A readiness API shall inspect a bounded caller-supplied descriptor set for read/write/error readiness and wait atomically to a deadline without consuming data.
rationale: Shell and worker loops need multiplexing without polling every device indefinitely.
acceptance: Oversized sets fail before driver calls; already-ready returns immediately; readiness transition between registration and sleep is not lost; closed/stale handles report per-entry error; timeout returns zero ready entries.
verification: Ready-before-wait, transition race, close race, invalid handle and maximum-set tests.
configuration: Optional readiness; configured maximum descriptors per wait.
resource_budget: One boot-reserved readiness record per waiting thread and bounded descriptor indices.
finding: Current yield/sleep APIs provide no multi-device readiness mechanism or atomic readiness wait.

title: Coherent device diagnostics
statement: Each driver shall expose a bounded typed health snapshot containing availability, fault reason, capacity/occupancy, overflow/error counts and reset generation without clearing counters on read.
rationale: Operators need to distinguish absent hardware, resource exhaustion and driver faults.
acceptance: Snapshots are internally coherent; counters saturate at maximum rather than wrap; repeated reads have no reset side effect; disabled features return not-supported; fixed output truncation reports required/written rows.
verification: Concurrent update/snapshot, saturation, disabled driver and bounded enumeration tests.
configuration: Optional device metrics with fixed per-driver schema and maximum snapshot rows.
resource_budget: Fixed per-device counters/state and caller-owned snapshot rows; no formatting under driver locks.
finding: Ethernet exposes unsynchronized owner-thread counters while thread snapshot reports required/written rows; no unified device health snapshot exists.
